title: Corporate Job vs Passion: Why She Chose Her Dream ?
description:
In this episode, we sit down with Ruchi, who made a bold decision to leave her corporate career after working with top companies like Infosys and pursue something deeply connected to her passion.

What started as a search for purpose turned into a unique business idea — creating 100% fruit-based healthy cakes that are gluten-free, vegan, and sugar-free.

In this conversation, we talk about:

✨ Transitioning from a corporate job to entrepreneurship
✨ Following your passion despite uncertainty
✨ Balancing motherhood and business
✨ The mindset required to build your own brand
✨ Gratitude, personal growth, and inner transformation

description:

    [01:44] Career Transition & Health Struggles: Disha discusses leaving a successful government job due to emotional exhaustion. She reveals she is a survivor of cancer during pregnancy and a brain tumor warrior, experiences that led her to discover her calling in healing.

title: Heartbreak Changed My Music: Dinesh Nautiyal on Divorce, Pain & 18 Years of Struggle
description:
What happens when heartbreak becomes music—and passion refuses to die even after 18 years of struggle?

In this emotional episode of The Attitude of Gratitude Podcast, host Sadhna sits down with Dinesh Nautiyal, a music composer, singer, lyricist, and independent artist, to uncover the real story behind his music journey.

From discovering his passion for singing at the age of 14–15 to balancing a demanding 9-to-5 corporate job as a Design Engineer with nearly 8 hours in the music studio, Dinesh's journey reveals the unseen reality of a struggling musician and the dedication required to pursue a creative dream.

Dinesh opens up about one of the most painful chapters of his life—his divorce—and how heartbreak deeply influenced his songwriting and music. He shares how personal pain, love, and real-life experiences became the inspiration behind some of his most emotional songs.

After an 18-year music journey, Dinesh has released two albums, reached around 8 lakh audio listeners, and gained over 2 lakh views on YouTube for his music. But his story is not about overnight success. It is about hard work, pure “Niyat” (intention), resilience, and climbing every step without shortcuts.

In this podcast, Dinesh Nautiyal talks about heartbreak and music inspiration, balancing a 9-to-5 job with passion, the reality of struggling musicians, independent artist life, songwriting from personal experiences, and the truth behind overnight success.

He also shares his plans to expand into Dubai and his vision to discover and support real, raw singing, writing, and music talent who may have passion but lack the right opportunities or financial backing.

From working two jobs during difficult times to dreaming of recording a song with his mother, this is a deeply personal conversation about music, pain, passion, gratitude, and never forgetting your roots.

If you are an aspiring singer, music composer, lyricist, independent artist, or someone struggling to balance your job and passion, this conversation is for you.

title: She Built a Brand Around ONE Word — SABR
description:
How do you turn patience into a fashion brand? Pooja Raval, founder of SABR in Dubai, built a purpose-led clothing brand around one powerful word: SABR — patience, resilience and the strength to keep moving before the results arrive.

Her journey to becoming a fashion entrepreneur was anything but linear.

Engineering in India. An MBA in Marketing. Experience in retail and FMCG. A move to the UK to study strategic marketing and consumer behaviour. Career uncertainty, the pressure of finding sponsorship, another move to Dubai — and eventually the decision to build something of her own.

That journey became the foundation of SABR.

Pooja didn't want to create another clothing label with a motivational word printed on a T-shirt. She wanted the clothing to become a reminder — especially for entrepreneurs, creators and people going through uncertain stages of life — that meaningful things take time.

The conversation goes deeper into the psychology behind the brand: why modern life has made us impatient, why comparison damages self-confidence, how self-acceptance changes the way we make decisions, and why patience without action isn't really SABR.

There is also a fascinating founder lesson here.

Before building the brand, Pooja started speaking about the idea of SABR at networking events and watching how people reacted to the word. Those conversations helped validate something bigger than the clothing itself: almost everyone could connect SABR to a personal chapter of their life.

And that is where the brand becomes interesting.

A mother waiting nine months.

An entrepreneur waiting for the business to work.

A creator waiting for the audience to grow.

Someone waiting for a career opportunity.

Someone starting again after failure.

Different journeys. The same need for SABR.

Pooja's vision extends beyond fashion into SABR Stories, founder collaborations, limited-edition drops and a community built around people's real experiences of patience and resilience.

Today, SABR describes itself as a UAE-born luxury clothing brand rooted in patience, heritage and limited releases, with the philosophy “Wear the Wait.” The brand's current identity connects patience with faith, strength, purpose, growth and legacy.

This conversation will particularly resonate if you watch content around entrepreneurship, women founders, Dubai business, fashion startups, clothing brand building, founder stories, personal branding, consumer psychology, self-development or purpose-driven businesses.

Because behind almost every success story is a period nobody sees:

the uncertainty,
the rejection,
the waiting,
the rebuilding,
and the decision to continue anyway.

Patience isn't doing nothing.
It's knowing when to wait — while continuing to work.

That is SABR.

Discover SABR

title: PCOS Weight Loss: Why You Can’t Lose Weight | Insulin Resistance Explained
description:
Struggling to lose weight with PCOS even when you’re trying to eat better and exercise?

In this episode of The Attitude of Gratitude, Sadhna Sharma sits down with Dr. Lamya Kamal to understand why PCOS can make weight management more complicated — and the important role insulin resistance may play.

Dr. Lamya shares both her medical perspective and her own personal experience with PCOS, weight struggles and body shaming. Together, they discuss why simply telling someone to “eat less” or “exercise more” may overlook the hormonal and metabolic factors behind their struggle.

This conversation explores PCOS/PCOD symptoms, insulin resistance, weight gain, diet and carbohydrates, along with practical discussions around roti, rice, protein and everyday food choices.

They also discuss different approaches used in PCOS management, including lifestyle changes, strength training and medical treatments such as Metformin, contraceptive pills and GLP-1 medications including Ozempic and Mounjaro.

The episode also touches on intermittent fasting, artificial sweeteners and why health advice should be personalised rather than copied from short social-media clips.

You’ll hear about common signs associated with PCOS such as irregular periods, acne, excess facial or body hair, dark skin patches and difficulty managing weight — as well as why PCOS is about much more than fertility alone.

Most importantly, this conversation challenges the shame surrounding women’s weight and hormonal health. Better health starts with understanding what is happening inside your body, finding the right support and following an approach that works for you.

Please watch the complete conversation before making major changes to your diet, medication or exercise routine, and consult a qualified healthcare professional for personalised medical advice.

If you found this conversation useful, share it with another woman — or with a husband, partner, brother, father or friend who wants to better understand women’s hormonal health.
